item.title: Flavio Bolsonaro expected to land in Miami shortly after Trump offers Brazil exit
item.description: RIO DE JANEIRO, Oct 28 - The plane believed to be carrying Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro and his family to the United States was scheduled to arrive on Wednesday morning in Miami, where they will be given entry visas by the United States government.
item.dc:creator: The Straits Times
item.content:encoded:
Flavio Bolsonaro expected to land in Miami shortly after Trump offers Brazil exit Sign up now: Get ST's newsletters delivered to your inbox

Brazilian presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro of the Liberal Party (PL) speaks after losing the presidential runoff election, in Brasilia, Brazil October 25, 2026. REUTERS/Adriano Machado

Published   Oct 28, 2026, 08:01 PM

Updated   Oct 28, 2026, 08:36 PM

Set as preferred source

Listen

RIO DE JANEIRO, Oct 28 - The plane believed to be carrying Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro and his family to the United States was scheduled to arrive on Wednesday morning in Miami, where they will be given entry visas by the United States government. With the whole world trying to work out where he was, Bolsonaro entered Argentina with his wife and two daughters late on Tuesday evening, according to the country's migration department. Bolsonaro, who lost Sunday's presidential election to leftist incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and had refused to comply with a Supreme Court order to hand over his passports, crossed into Argentina via the Tancredo Neves International Bridge, about 19 hours by road from his home in Brasilia.

The family then boarded a private plane operated by Baires Fly S.A. bound for the Ecuadorean city of Guayaquil, the migration department said. Argentina's presidency did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Neither did Baires Fly. A Gulfstream G400 operated by Baires Fly, registration LV-JQW, departed Puerto Iguazu at 12:22 a.m. (0322 GMT) and landed in Guayaquil at 3:46 a.m. (0846 GMT), according to FlightAware. The aircraft then departed for Miami's Opa-locka Executive Airport, where it was scheduled to land at 9:18 a.m. local time (1318 GMT).

It was unclear how Bolsonaro entered Ecuador. Authorities there did not immediately respond to a request for comment. FRESH BRAZIL-US RIFT Bolsonaro's departure threatens to deepen a rift between the two most populous nations in the Americas.

Lula has accused Washington of colluding with the Bolsonaro family to help return them to power. Ahead of Sunday's election, Reuters reported on a US State Department campaign to restore the Bolsonaros to office. Trump told reporters on Wednesday that he would approve of Bolsonaro coming to the United States, after his State Department said it would give them entry visas. Trump has previously alleged that Flavio's father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, was a victim of judicial persecution in Brazil. Jair Bolsonaro also travelled to the United States after refusing to concede defeat to Lula in 2022, during Joe Biden's presidency. He eventually returned but was later given a 27-year sentence for plotting a coup after his supporters stormed government buildings in Brasilia. Bolsonaro had been favored to win Sunday's presidential election but ended up losing in a shock result. Bolsonaro, who loses his immunity from prosecution when his Senate term ends in February, had said on Monday after the order to hand in his passports that he had no plans to flee. "I have never thought about leaving the country," he said. "I will hand over my passports and defend myself against this travesty, which is a clear attempt to intimidate me." REUTERS

item.title: US tells ships to avoid unnecessary transits through Hormuz
item.description: It remains unclear what prompted the advisory.
item.dc:creator: The Straits Times
item.content:encoded:
US tells ships to avoid unnecessary transits through Hormuz Sign up now: Get ST's newsletters delivered to your inbox

The US military last publicly issued a similar notice in mid-July, when it began its blockade of Iranian shipping. PHOTO: REUTERS

Published   Oct 28, 2026, 08:00 PM

Updated   Oct 28, 2026, 09:18 PM

Set as preferred source

Listen Summarise

The US told ships to avoid unnecessary trips through the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf of Oman because of rising regional tensions and possible delays. The advisory said vessels may face questioning, visits and searches to confirm their intentions under the US blockade of Iran. Oil traffic has recovered near prewar levels, but Iran has raised ship attacks to a wartime high of almost 30 in October, Bloomberg said.

AI generated

The US military said vessels that have no need to move between ports in the Gulf of Oman and the Strait of Hormuz should stay away, as tensions ratchet up in the region . “Due to the current geopolitical situation, vessels which do not need to transit the area are advised to remain well clear to avoid unnecessary delays to their voyage,” the US Naval Forces Central Command said in an advisory on Oct 28 issued via the Joint Maritime Information Center.  “Vessels transiting this area are advised to plan additional transit time to allow for increased traffic density and military blockade enforcement operations,” the notice said.

It remains unclear what prompted the advisory. The US military last publicly issued a similar notice in mid-July, when it began its blockade of Iranian shipping . Back then, it said that the blockade would not impede neutral passage through Hormuz, though ships should expect to be questioned on their intentions. Traffic through the chokepoint has recovered in recent months, with shuttle tankers making up a big part of the traffic carrying crude oil. These ships make multiple runs in and out of the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman, where other tankers unwilling to risk the Strait await to receive cargoes. Dozens of crude tankers willing to take the risk have helped lift oil flows from the Persian Gulf to near prewar levels, while the US blockade has pushed Iranian crude exports close to zero. At the same time, Iran has been ramping up its attacks on ships to a wartime high of almost 30 in October.

The latest US advisory said that neutral vessels with neutral cargo or are in ballast sailing between these neutral ports may be subject to questioning, visit, and search to confirm their intentions regarding the blockade. The US Central Command and the US Naval Forces Central Command – the naval unit that is part of Centcom and oversees the naval blockade of Iran – did not immediately respond to an emailed request for comment.
